questionText: Despite his best efforts, he could not secure a promotion because he was found wanting _____ dedication.
explanation:
The phrase 'wanting in' means lacking or deficient in a particular quality. Here, it means lacking dedication.
उदा. 'Wanting in' एक निश्चित गुण की कमी को दर्शाता है। यहाँ समर्पण (dedication) की कमी का अर्थ है, इसलिए 'in' सही preposition है।

questionText: The manager asked the employees to refrain _____ using mobile phones during the meeting.
explanation:
The verb 'refrain' is always followed by the preposition 'from' to indicate stopping oneself from doing something.
उदा. Verb 'refrain' के बाद हमेशा preposition 'from' का प्रयोग होता है, जिसका अर्थ किसी कार्य को करने से बचना है।

questionText: Had the police arrived on time, the tragedy _____ prevented.
explanation:
This is a third conditional sentence in the past. The structure for past unreal condition is 'If + subject + had + V3, subject + would/could/might + have + V3'.
उदा. यह Third Conditional वाक्य है। भूतकाल की असंभावित शर्त के लिए 'Had + V3' के साथ मुख्य खंड में 'could have been + V3' का प्रयोग होता है।

questionText: Her views on the new economic policy do not _____ with mine.
explanation:
'Coincide with' means to correspond or agree exactly with something. Her views match or agree with mine.
उदा. 'Coincide with' का अर्थ विचारों या मत का मेल खाना होता है।

questionText: The government has implemented stringent measures to _____ corruption in public offices.
explanation:
'Curb' means to restrain or control something undesirable, like corruption.
उदा. 'Curb' का अर्थ किसी बुरी चीज़ (जैसे भ्रष्टाचार) पर अंकुश लगाना या नियंत्रित करना होता है।

questionText: Scarcely had he stepped out of the house _____ it began to rain heavily.
explanation:
The correlative conjunction 'Scarcely' or 'Hardly' is always followed by 'when' or 'before', whereas 'No sooner' is followed by 'than'.
उदा. 'Scarcely' या 'Hardly' के साथ हमेशा 'when' का प्रयोग किया जाता है, जबकि 'No sooner' के साथ 'than' आता है।

questionText: Neither the teacher nor the students _____ present in the class room.
explanation:
According to the rule of Subject-Verb Agreement, when two subjects are joined by 'neither... nor', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. Here 'students' is plural, so plural verb 'were' is used.
उदा. जब दो Subject 'neither... nor' से जुड़े हों, तो verb अपने पास वाले Subject के अनुसार आती है। 'students' plural है, इसलिए 'were' आएगा।

questionText: The scientist spent years trying to _____ the complex mystery of the universe.
explanation:
'Unravel' means to investigate and solve or explain something complicated or mysterious like a mystery.
उदा. 'Unravel' का अर्थ किसी रहस्य या जटिल समस्या को सुलझाना या स्पष्ट करना होता है।

questionText: Only by working persistently day and night _____ achieve success in this competitive exam.
explanation:
When a sentence begins with a negative or limiting adverbial expression like 'Only by', inversion is required (Auxiliary verb comes before the subject).
उदा. जब वाक्य की शुरुआत 'Only by' जैसे वाक्यांश से होती है, तो inversion नियम के अनुसार Helping Verb (can) Subject (you) से पहले आती है।

questionText: The pioneer of artificial intelligence warned that unchecked technological growth could pose a threat to human _____.
explanation:
'Human existence' is a standard collocation referring to the survival or state of living for human beings.
उदा. 'Human existence' का अर्थ मानव अस्तित्व या जीवन से है, जो AI के खतरे के संदर्भ में बिल्कुल सटीक बैठता है।

questionText: She has been working on this research project _______ three months.
explanation:
Use 'for' to denote a period of time (three months). Use 'since' for a point of time.
उदा. निश्चित समय (point of time) के लिए 'since' और अनिश्चित अवधि (period of time) के लिए 'for' का प्रयोग किया जाता है।

questionText: Hardly had he stepped out of the house _______ it started raining heavily.
explanation:
The correlative conjunction for 'Hardly' or 'Scarcely' is always 'when'.
उदा. 'Hardly' या 'Scarcely' के साथ हमेशा 'when' का प्रयोग होता है, जबकि 'No sooner' के साथ 'than' आता है।

questionText: Despite working hard, he could not succeed because he lacked _______ guidance.
explanation:
In the context of lacking direction or advice, 'proper' guidance is the most appropriate collocation.
उदा. सही दिशा या सलाह न मिलने के संदर्भ में 'proper guidance' (उचित मार्गदर्शन) सबसे उपयुक्त शब्द है।

questionText: Neither the manager nor his subordinates _______ present at the meeting yesterday.
explanation:
When two subjects are joined by 'neither... nor', the verb agrees with the subject nearest to it. Here, 'subordinates' is plural, so 'were' is used.
उदा. जब दो कर्ता 'neither... nor' से जुड़े हों, तो क्रिया (verb) अपने सबसे पास वाले कर्ता के अनुसार आती है। यहाँ 'subordinates' बहुवचन है, अतः 'were' आएगा।

questionText: The police are looking _______ the matter to find the culprit.
explanation:
The phrasal verb 'look into' means to investigate a matter.
उदा. फ्रेजल वर्ब 'look into' का अर्थ किसी मामले की जांच करना (investigate) होता है।

questionText: Had I known about the traffic jam, I _______ another route.
explanation:
In third conditional sentences expressing past hypothetical situations, the structure is 'Had + subject + V3, subject + would have + V3'.
उदा. भूतकाल की अवास्तविक स्थिति (Third Conditional) में 'Had + V3' के साथ मुख्य खंड में 'would have + V3' का प्रयोग किया जाता है।

questionText: The rapid advancement of technology has made our lives much more _______.
explanation:
An adjective is required after the verb 'made' and its object 'our lives' to act as an object complement. 'Convenient' is an adjective.
उदा. वर्ब 'made' और ऑब्जेक्ट 'our lives' के बाद विशेषता बताने के लिए एडजेक्टिव (Adjective) की आवश्यकता होती है।

questionText: A grand reception will be _______ in honor of the winning cricket team.
explanation:
We use the verb 'hold' (held in past/passive) to indicate hosting an event, meeting, or reception.
उदा. किसी समारोह, सभा या रिसेप्शन के आयोजन के लिए 'hold' वर्ब का प्रयोग किया जाता है।

questionText: Only one of the students _______ selected for the national scholarship program.
explanation:
The structure 'One of + plural noun' takes a singular verb because the subject is 'One'.
उदा. 'One of + plural noun' के बाद हमेशा एकवचन (singular) वर्ब का प्रयोग होता है क्योंकि मुख्य कर्ता 'One' होता है।

questionText: His speech was so _______ that the audience remained spellbound through out.
explanation:
Since the audience remained 'spellbound' (मंत्रमुग्ध), the speech must have been captivating (fascinating/attractive).
उदा. चूँकि श्रोता 'spellbound' (मंत्रमुग्ध) थे, इसलिए भाषण निश्चित रूप से 'captivating' (आकर्षक) रहा होगा।

questionText: Identify the word that is incorrectly spelled
explanation:
"Preposterous" is the correct spelling with a single "p" after the first "r". The root word is "posterous".
उदाहरण: "बेवकूफी" के लिए "preposterous" सही शब्द है।

questionText: I have been looking forward _____ see you next week.
explanation:
Rule: The phrase is "look forward to" + noun/verb-ing. Example: *I have been looking forward to seeing you.*
उदाहरण: *मैं अगले हफ़्ते तुम्हें देखने के लिए उत्सुक हूँ.*

questionText: He was known _____ his punctuality.
explanation:
Rule: The adjective *known* is followed by *for* when stating a reputation. Example: *He was known for his punctuality.*
उदाहरण: *उसे अपनी समयबद्धता के लिए जाना जाता है.*

questionText: The company is planning _____ expand its operations into Asia.
explanation:
Rule: The verb *plan* is followed by *to* + base form of verb. Example: *They plan to expand.*
उदाहरण: *कंपनी अपनी संचालन को एशिया में विस्तारित करने की योजना बना रही है.*

questionText: The meeting was ___ due to the unforeseen circumstances.
explanation:
Rule: Past participle *cancelled* is used after a past tense verb. Example: *The meeting was cancelled.*
उदाहरण: *अनपेक्षित परिस्थितियों के कारण बैठक रद्द कर दी गई.*

questionText: The house was built ___ 1920.
explanation:
Rule: The preposition *in* is used with years. Example: *built in 1920.*
उदाहरण: *घर 1920 में बनाया गया था.*

questionText: She was praised _____ her bravery during the rescue.
explanation:
Rule: The verb *praise* is followed by *for* when indicating a reason. Example: *praised for her bravery.*
उदाहरण: *उसे बचाव के दौरान उसकी बहादुरी के लिए प्रशंसा की गई.*

questionText: By the time the train arrived, the passengers ____.
explanation:
Rule: Past perfect simple (had + past participle) describes an action completed before another past event. Example: *by the time the train arrived, they had boarded.*
उदाहरण: *ट्रेन आने तक, यात्री पहले ही चढ़ चुके थे.*

questionText: The project was delayed _____ lack of resources.
explanation:
Rule: *due to* is followed by a noun phrase or gerund to express reason. Example: *delayed due to lack of resources.*
उदाहरण: *संसाधनों की कमी के कारण परियोजना विलंबित हुई.*

questionText: She is ___ for her artistic talent.
explanation:
Rule: The adjective *known* is used to indicate reputation. Example: *She is known for her talent.*
उदाहरण: *वह अपनी कलात्मक प्रतिभा के लिए जानी जाती है.*

questionText: We will start the project _____ the first quarter of 2024.
explanation:
Rule: The preposition *in* is used with a quarter or month. Example: *in the first quarter.*
उदाहरण: *हम परियोजना को प्रथम तिमाही 2024 में शुरू करेंगे.*

questionText: The committee will discuss the proposal _____ the next meeting.
explanation:
Rule: The preposition *in* is used with meetings or events in time. Example: *in the next meeting.*
उदाहरण: *समिति अगली बैठक में प्रस्ताव पर चर्चा करेगी.*

questionText: Choose the correctly spelled term
explanation:
The correct spelling is necessary, with ‘e’ after ‘n’. 
उदा. सही वर्तनी: necessary.
यह शब्द अक्सर ‘necessary’ के रूप में लिखा जाता है।

questionText: She is knowing the truth about the incident since last week.
explanation:
Verbs of perception or state (like know, understand, belong) are generally not used in continuous tenses. When used with 'since', they take the present perfect tense.
उदा. 'Know' जैसे Stative verbs का प्रयोग continuous tense में नहीं होता। 'Since' के साथ समय दिखाने के लिए Present Perfect Tense ('has known') का प्रयोग किया जाता है।

questionText: Neither the teacher nor the students was present in the class.
explanation:
When two subjects are joined by 'neither... nor', the verb agrees with the subject nearest to it. Here, 'students' is plural, so the verb must be plural ('were').
उदा. जब दो सब्जेक्ट्स 'neither... nor' से जुड़े हों, तो वर्ब अपने सबसे पास वाले सब्जेक्ट के अनुसार आती है। यहाँ 'students' बहुवचन है, अतः 'were' आएगा।

questionText: The principal asked the monitor to distribute the sweets between all the students.
explanation:
'Between' is used for two objects/persons, while 'among' is used for more than two. Since there are 'all the students' (more than two), 'among' is correct.
उदा. दो से अधिक व्यक्तियों या वस्तुओं के लिए 'among' का प्रयोग होता है, जबकि 'between' केवल दो के लिए आता है।

questionText: If I was you, I would never accept such a humiliating offer.
explanation:
In conditional sentences expressing an imaginary situation or unreal present, 'were' is used with all subjects, including singular pronouns like 'I'.
उदा. काल्पनिक वाक्यों (Imaginative sentences) में सभी सब्जेक्ट्स के साथ 'I' के बाद भी 'were' का प्रयोग होता है, 'was' का नहीं।

questionText: One of the most efficient worker in our office has been promoted.
explanation:
The phrase 'One of' is always followed by a plural noun and a singular verb. Therefore, 'worker' must be changed to 'workers'.
उदा. 'One of the' के बाद हमेशा Noun बहुवचन (Plural noun) फॉर्म में होता है, लेकिन Verb एकवचन (Singular) होती है। इसलिए 'worker' की जगह 'workers' होगा।

questionText: He insisted to accompany me to the railway station despite my refusal.
explanation:
The verb 'insist' is always followed by the preposition 'on' and a gerund (V1+ing).
उदा. 'Insist' वर्ब के बाद हमेशा प्रीपोजिशन 'on' और उसके बाद Gerund (V1+ing) यानी 'accompanying' का प्रयोग होता है।

questionText: She speaks English with a fluent accent, which impresses every one.
explanation:
An adverb is required to modify how someone speaks. 'Fluently' is the correct adverb replacing the adjective 'fluent' modifying the verb 'speaks'.
उदा. वर्ब ('speaks') की विशेषता बताने के लिए Adjective ('fluent') की जगह Adverb ('fluently') का प्रयोग होना चाहिए।

questionText: The manager as well as his subordinates were blamed for the financial loss.
explanation:
When subjects are connected by 'as well as', the verb agrees with the first subject ('The manager', which is singular). Hence, 'were' should be replaced by 'was'.
उदा. जब दो सब्जेक्ट्स 'as well as' से जुड़ते हैं, तो वर्ब पहले सब्जेक्ट के अनुसार आती है। 'The manager' एकवचन है, इसलिए 'were' की जगह 'was' आएगा।

questionText: Hardly had I stepped out of the house *when it started raining* heavily.
explanation:
The correlative conjunction for 'Hardly/Scarcely' is 'when' (or 'before'), not 'than'. Therefore, the original sentence is grammatically correct.
उदा. 'Hardly' या 'Scarcely' के साथ हमेशा 'when' का प्रयोग किया जाता है, 'than' का नहीं (जो कि 'No sooner' के साथ आता है)। इसलिए दिया गया वाक्य सही है।

questionText: She is *more taller than* her sister by two inches.
explanation:
Double comparatives ('more taller') are grammatically incorrect in English. Use the single comparative form 'taller'.
उदा. एक ही वाक्य में दो comparative words ('more' और '-er') का एक साथ प्रयोग गलत है। सही रूप 'taller than' होगा।

questionText: If I was you, *I would not trust* him with my money.
options: I were you, I would not trust
If I were you, I would not trust
explanation:
In conditional sentences expressing an imaginary or unreal situation, 'were' is used with all subjects, including singular pronouns like 'I'.
उदा. काल्पनिक वाक्यों (Subjunctive mood) में कर्ता चाहे कोई भी हो, 'was' के स्थान पर हमेशा 'were' का प्रयोग किया जाता है।

questionText: The manager asked the employee *why was he late* for the important meeting.
explanation:
In indirect speech or embedded questions, the sentence structure changes from interrogative (verb + subject) to assertive (subject + verb).
उदा. Indirect speech या embedded question में प्रश्नसूचक शब्द के बाद पहले Subject आता है और फिर Verb (why he was late), न कि 'why was he late'।
grammarRule: Direct to Indirect / Embedded Question Structure

questionText: Each of the students *were given* a prize for their outstanding performance.
explanation:
The pronouns 'Each', 'Everyone', 'Either', etc., take a singular verb because they refer to individuals separately.
उदा. 'Each' के साथ हमेशा Singular Verb ('was') का प्रयोग होता है, भले ही इसके बाद आने वाला noun plural हो।

questionText: No sooner did the police arrive *when the thieves fled* from the scene.
explanation:
The correlative conjunction for 'No sooner' is always 'than', not 'when' or 'then'.
उदा. 'No sooner' के साथ हमेशा 'than' का प्रयोग होता है, 'when' का नहीं।

questionText: She has *a great passion for* music and painting.
explanation:
The noun 'passion' is correctly followed by the preposition 'for' when expressing enthusiasm for something.
उदा. 'Passion' शब्द के साथ उचित प्रीपोज़िशन 'for' का प्रयोग होता है। वाक्य में कोई सुधार की आवश्यकता नहीं है।

questionText: He told me that he *has completed* his graduation two years ago.
explanation:
When the reporting verb is in the past tense ('told') and the reported speech contains a past time marker ('two years ago'), the tense changes to Past Perfect ('had completed').
उदा. वाक्य में 'two years ago' भूतकाल के समय को दर्शाता है और मुख्य क्लॉज past tense में है, इसलिए Present Perfect ('has completed') की जगह Past Perfect ('had completed') आएगा।

questionText: Despite of working hard, *he failed to secure* good marks in the examination.
explanation:
'Despite' is never followed by 'of'. (Note: 'In spite' takes 'of'). Therefore, 'Despite working hard' is correct.
उदा. 'Despite' के साथ कभी भी 'of' का प्रयोग नहीं होता है (जबकि 'In spite' के साथ 'of' आता है)। अतः सही विकल्प 'Despite working hard' है।
grammarRule: Preposition Usage (Despite vs In spite of)

questionText: Neither the teacher nor the students *was present* in the class room.
explanation:
When two subjects are joined by 'neither... nor', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. Here, 'students' is plural, so 'were' should be used.
उदा. जब दो सब्जेक्ट्स 'neither... nor' से जुड़े हों, तो वर्ब अपने सबसे नज़दीकी सब्जेक्ट के अनुसार आती है। यहाँ 'students' (Plural) के अनुसार 'were' आएगा।

questionText: The committee (underlined) had decided to postpone the meeting.
options: has decided to postpone the meeting,
had decided to postpone the meeting,
explanation:
The past tense ‘decided’ correctly conveys the action already completed. Using ‘has decided’ changes the tense to present perfect which is inappropriate here. 
उदाहरण: The committee decided to postpone the meeting.

questionText: She (underlined) had been working there for five years before she left.
explanation:
The correct form is ‘had been working’ to show continuous action in the past before another past event. 
उदाहरण: She had been working there for five years before she left.
grammarRule: Underlined phrase replacement – past perfect continuous

questionText: The report (underlined) was submitted on time, but the manager was not satisfied.
explanation:
The passive form ‘was submitted’ correctly indicates the action performed by someone else. 
उदाहरण: The report was submitted on time.

questionText: If I (underlined) had known about the traffic, I would have taken a different route.
explanation:
The conditional perfect ‘had known’ correctly matches the third conditional structure. 
उदाहरण: If I had known, I would have taken a different route.

questionText: During the meeting, the chair man (underlined) emphasized the importance of punctuality.
explanation:
The simple past ‘emphasized’ is correct for a completed action in the past. 
उदाहरण: He emphasized the point.

questionText: The new policy (underlined) will be implemented next month.
explanation:
The future passive ‘will be implemented’ correctly indicates a future action. 
उदाहरण: The policy will be implemented next month.

questionText: Despite the rain (underlined) the match continued as scheduled.
explanation:
The correct adverbial clause is ‘rain’, which directly refers to the weather condition. 
उदाहरण: Despite the rain, the match continued.

questionText: Every student (underlined) should submit their assignments by Friday.
explanation:
The modal ‘must’ expresses a mandatory requirement. 
उदाहरण: Every student must submit their assignments by Friday.

questionText: The committee (underlined) has decided to postpone the meeting until next week.
explanation:
The present perfect ‘has decided’ correctly indicates a decision made earlier that affects the present. 
उदाहरण: The committee has decided.

questionText: By the time the train (underlined) arrived, the passengers had already boarded.
explanation:
The simple past ‘arrived’ correctly matches the past perfect ‘had boarded’ in the second clause. 
उदाहरण: By the time the train arrived, the passengers had boarded.

questionText: Select the option that has the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
explanation:
The correct spelling is 'Niece'. The rule 'i before e except after c' applies here.
उदा. 'Niece' की सही स्पेलिंग 'n-i-e-c-e' है, न कि 'neice'।
grammarRule: I before E except after C

questionText: The committee has decided to postpone the meeting until next week because of the unavailability of the key members.
options: The committee has decided to postpone the meeting until next week because of the key members’ unavailability.
The committee has decided to postpone the meeting until next week because of the unavailability of the key members.
The committee has decided to postpone the meeting until next week because of the key members’ availability.
explanation:
The correct option replaces the phrase ‘unavailability of the key members’ with the possessive form ‘key members’ unavailability’, which is more concise and idiomatic.
उदाहरण: 'key members’ unavailability' अंग्रेज़ी में सही और स्वाभाविक है।

questionText: She has been working as a teacher for ten years, which has made her very experienced in handling diverse student groups.
options: She has been working as a teacher for ten years, which has made her very experienced in handling diverse student groups.
She has been working as a teacher for ten years, which has made her very experienced at handling diverse student groups.
explanation:
The phrase ‘in handling’ is replaced by ‘at handling’, which is the correct preposition with ‘experienced’.
उदाहरण: 'experienced at handling' सही है।

questionText: The new policy, which aims to reduce carbon emissions, will be implemented next month.
options: The new policy, which aims to reduce carbon emissions, will be implemented next month.
The new policy, which aims to decrease carbon emissions, will be implemented next month.
explanation:
The adjective ‘reduce’ is more appropriate with ‘carbon emissions’ than ‘decrease’, making the sentence more precise.
उदाहरण: ‘reduce carbon emissions’ अधिक सामान्य है।

questionText: He was known for his punctuality and his dedication to the work, which earned him a promotion.
options: He was known for his punctuality and his dedication to the work, which earned him a promotion.
explanation:
The phrase ‘which earned him a promotion’ should be replaced by ‘which earned him a promotion’ for correct relative pronoun usage.
उदाहरण: ‘which earned him a promotion’ सही है।

questionText: The project was completed ahead of schedule, which made the team extremely proud of their achievement.
options: The project was completed ahead of schedule, which made the team extremely proud of their achievement.
explanation:
The phrase ‘extremely proud of their achievement’ is best kept as is; the other options do not improve the sentence.
उदाहरण: ‘extremely proud of their achievement’ सही है।

questionText: The manager has requested the employees to submit their reports by Friday, which should be done by the end of the week.
options: The manager has requested the employees to submit their reports by Friday, which should be done by the end of the week.
The manager has requested the employees to submit their reports by Friday, which should be completed by the end of the week.
explanation:
Replacing ‘done’ with ‘completed’ gives a more formal tone appropriate for managerial context.
उदाहरण: ‘completed by the end of the week’ अधिक औपचारिक है।

questionText: The new manager’s policy, which encourages team work has significantly improved the work place environment.
options: The new manager’s policy, which encourages teamwork, has significantly improved the workplace environment.
explanation:
The phrase ‘which encourages teamwork’ is correctly placed as a non‑restrictive clause; no change needed.
उदाहरण: ‘which encourages teamwork’ सही है।

questionText: He has studied medicine for many years, which has made his knowledge extremely comprehensive.
options: He has studied medicine for many years, which has made his knowledge extremely comprehensive.
explanation:
The word ‘extremely’ is better placed before ‘comprehensive’ to emphasize the degree.
उदाहरण: ‘extremely comprehensive’ उपयुक्त है।

questionText: The company’s new product, which is expected to be a hit in the market, will launch next month.
options: The company’s new product, which is expected to be a hit in the market, will launch next month.
explanation:
The sentence is already grammatically correct; the phrase ‘expected to be a hit’ is appropriately used.
उदाहरण: ‘expected to be a hit’ सही है।

questionText: The research findings, which were published last week, have provided significant insights into climate change.
options: The research findings, which were published last week, have provided significant insights into climate change.
explanation:
The phrase ‘have provided significant insights’ correctly matches the plural subject ‘findings’.
उदाहरण: ‘have provided’ सही है।

questionText: The new policy, which has been announced by the government, aims to reduce pollution.
options: that was announced by the government
which is announced by the government
that has been announced by the government
which was announced by the government
explanation:
The relative clause refers to a past event, so the simple past ‘was announced’ is preferable to the present perfect. 
उदाहरण: The new policy, which was announced by the government, aims to reduce pollution.
grammarRule: Relative clause – simple past for past events

questionText: The committee, which is expected to meet next month, has already decided on the budget.
options: that is expected to meet next month
which has decided on the budget
explanation:
The clause should correctly express the future expectation; ‘is expected to meet’ is the best choice. 
उदाहरण: The committee, that is expected to meet next month, has already decided on the budget.

questionText: The book, which was written by a famous author, has sold over a million copies.
options: which was written by a famous writer
that was written by a famous author
which has written by a famous author
that was written by a famous writer
explanation:
The relative pronoun should be ‘that’ when it refers to a single object and the clause is a simple past. 
उदाहरण: The book, that was written by a famous author, has sold over a million copies.

questionText: The city, which is known for its festivals, attracts tourists from all over the world.
options: which is famous for its festivals
that is known for its festivals
which is known for its festivals
that is famous for its festivals
explanation:
Both ‘which’ and ‘that’ can be used, but the clause is correctly expressed with the simple present ‘is known’. 
उदाहरण: The city, which is known for its festivals, attracts tourists from all over the world.
grammarRule: Relative clause – simple present for general truth

questionText: The team, which had been practicing for months, finally won the championship.
options: which has been practicing for months
that had been practicing for months
explanation:
The past perfect ‘had been practicing’ correctly indicates the action completed before the win. 
उदाहरण: The team, that had been practicing for months, finally won the championship.
grammarRule: Past perfect for completed action before another past event

questionText: The report, which will be released on Monday, contains detailed statistics.
options: which will be released on Monday
explanation:
The clause correctly uses the future passive ‘will be released’. 
उदाहरण: The report, which will be released on Monday, contains detailed statistics.

questionText: The scientist, who had suggested a new theory, was recognized by the academy.
options: who had suggested a new theory
who has suggested a new theory
explanation:
Past perfect ‘had suggested’ correctly marks the action before recognition. 
उदाहरण: The scientist, who had suggested a new theory, was recognized by the academy.

questionText: The artwork, which was created during the Renaissance, is admired world wide.
options: which has been created during the Renaissance
which was created during the Renaissance
which is created during the Renaissance
which was creating during the Renaissance
explanation:
The simple past ‘was created’ correctly indicates the time of creation. 
उदाहरण: The artwork, which was created during the Renaissance, is admired worldwide.

questionText: The company, which has recently expanded its operations, plans to open new offices.
options: which is recently expanding its operations
which has recently expanded its operations
explanation:
The present perfect ‘has recently expanded’ correctly conveys a recent completion. 
उदाहरण: The company, which has recently expanded its operations, plans to open new offices.

questionText: The athlete, who had trained for years, broke the world record.
explanation:
Past perfect ‘had trained’ indicates training completed before the record. 
उदाहरण: The athlete, who had trained for years, broke the world record.

questionText: Select the correct spelling among the options.
explanation:
'Renaissance' is correctly spelled with single 'n', 'ai', and '-s-s-a-n-c-e'.
उदा. 'Renaissance' में सिंगल 'n', 'ai', और '-s-s-a-n-c-e' का सही प्रयोग होता है।

questionText: He stopped the meeting ___, because a senior officer had arrived.
explanation:
Rule: Use an adverb to modify the verb. The correct adverb is "abruptly".
उदाहरण: "उसे अचानक बैठक रोकनी पड़ी क्योंकि…"

questionText: The committee will consider the proposal ___.
explanation:
Rule: The adverb "carefully" should directly modify the verb phrase. The correct wording is "carefully in a manner".
उदाहरण: "समिति प्रस्ताव पर सावधानीपूर्वक विचार करेगी…"

questionText: He managed ___ his responsibilities effectively.
explanation:
Rule: After the verb "manage", a gerund is used to indicate the action performed. Thus "balancing" is correct.
उदाहरण: "उसने अपनी जिम्मेदारियों को संतुलित करने का प्रबंध किया…"

questionText: The book, ___ by the author, has been widely praised.
explanation:
Rule: Use the past participle to form a passive clause. "Written by" is correct.
उदाहरण: "किताब को लेखक ने लिखा है और इसे व्यापक प्रशंसा मिली है…"

questionText: She could not attend the conference, ___ she was ill.
explanation:
Rule: Use the conjunction "because" to express reason. "Because of" is a preposition phrase and does not fit here.
उदाहरण: "वह सम्मेलन में नहीं जा सकी क्योंकि वह बीमार थी…"

questionText: The new policy ___ to reduce costs.
explanation:
Rule: After the verb "aims", the infinitive form "to reduce" follows. "Aims at" is incorrect in this context.
उदाहरण: "नई नीति लागत घटाने का लक्ष्य रखती है…"

questionText: The students, ___ to the exam, studied diligently.
explanation:
Rule: Use the preposition "for" after "prepared" when referring to an event. Hence "prepared for" is correct.
उदाहरण: "छात्रों ने परीक्षा के लिए तैयारी की और कड़ी मेहनत की…"

questionText: He was praised ___ his efforts.
explanation:
Rule: The preposition "for" follows the verb "praised" to indicate the cause of praise. "For for" is redundant.
उदाहरण: "उसे उसके प्रयासों के लिए प्रशंसा मिली…"

questionText: The painting, ___ by the artist, was displayed.
explanation:
Rule: Use the past participle "exhibited" with "by" to form a passive clause. "Exhibited by the" is over‑specified.
उदाहरण: "कलाकार द्वारा प्रदर्शित पेंटिंग को दर्शकों ने सराहा…"

questionText: She will finish the report ___.
explanation:
Rule: The idiomatic phrase "on time" means punctual. "In time" has a different meaning and "at time" is incorrect.
उदाहरण: "वह रिपोर्ट समय पर पूरा करेगी…"

questionText: Identify the misspelled word in the following sentence: "Please definate that the meeting is scheduled.
explanation:
"Definate" is a common misspelling of "definitely", which means surely or without doubt.
उदाहरण: "She is definately the best candidate."

questionText: Identify the incorrectly spelled word in the list
explanation:
"Receive" is spelled with 'e' before 'i' when followed by a 'c': 'c' + 'e' + 'i'.
उदाहरण: "Please receive the package."
grammarRule: Rule of 'i before e except after c'

questionText: Hardly had I stepped out / of the house when a heavy downpour / started and drenched me completely. / No error
explanation:
No error. 'Hardly' is correctly followed by 'had + subject + V3' and the clause is connected with 'when'. 
उदा. इस वाक्य में 'Hardly' के साथ 'had' और 'when' का सही प्रयोग किया गया है। अतः कोई त्रुटि नहीं है।

questionText: One of my friends are / leaving for New York / next week to attend a seminar. / No error
explanation:
Replace 'are' with 'is'. The structure 'One of + plural noun' takes a singular verb. 
उदा. 'One of' के बाद plural noun आता है लेकिन verb हमेशा singular (is) होती है क्योंकि subject 'One' है।

questionText: Neither the teacher nor the students / was present in the auditorium / when the principal arrived. / No error
explanation:
Replace 'was' with 'were'. When subjects are joined by 'neither... nor', the verb agrees with the closer subject ('students', which is plural). 
उदा. 'Neither... nor' से जुड़ने पर verb पास वाले subject ('students') के अनुसार plural (were) होगी।

questionText: She is more smarter / than her sister / in solving complex puzzles. / No error
explanation:
Remove 'more'. Double comparatives ('more smarter') are grammatically incorrect. Use 'smarter'. 
उदा. एक साथ दो comparative words ('more' और '-er') का प्रयोग नहीं किया जाता है।

questionText: The manager asked the employee / why did he reach late / to the office on Monday. / No error
explanation:
Change 'why did he reach' to 'why he reached'. In indirect/reported questions, the sentence structure is Subject + Verb, not interrogative. 
उदा. Indirect speech या clause में प्रश्नवाचक वाक्य का क्रम नहीं, बल्कि Subject + Verb (he reached) का प्रयोग होता है।
grammarRule: Direct and Indirect Speech / Word Order

questionText: Not only the professor / but also his assistants was / involved in the research project. / No error
explanation:
Replace 'was' with 'were'. With 'not only... but also', the verb agrees with the subject closer to it ('assistants', plural). 
उदा. 'Not only... but also' में verb नजदीक वाले subject ('assistants') के अनुसार plural होगी।

questionText: Despite of working hard / through the night, Rohit / failed to clear the exam. / No error
explanation:
Remove 'of'. 'Despite' is never followed by 'of', whereas 'In spite' takes 'of'. 
उदा. 'Despite' के साथ कभी भी 'of' का प्रयोग नहीं होता है (In spite of होता है)।

questionText: If I was the king of this country, / I would eradicate poverty / and ensure equal rights for all. / No error
explanation:
Replace 'was' with 'were'. In hypothetical (imaginary) sentences, 'were' is used with all subjects. 
उदा. काल्पनिक वाक्यों (Subjunctive mood) में सभी subjects के साथ 'were' का प्रयोग होता है, 'was' का नहीं।

questionText: She has been living in this city / for five years / when her parents shifted here. / No error
explanation:
Replace 'has been living' with 'had been living'. Since the second clause is in past tense ('shifted'), the first clause must denote a past continuous duration (Past Perfect Continuous). 
उदा. वाक्य का दूसरा भाग past tense में है, इसलिए पहला भाग भी past perfect continuous ('had been living') में होना चाहिए।

questionText: Each of the participants / were given a certificate / at the end of the work shop / No error
explanation:
Replace 'were' with 'was'. 'Each' is singular and takes a singular verb. 
उदा. 'Each of' के बाद plural noun आता है, लेकिन verb हमेशा singular (was) होती है क्योंकि मुख्य subject 'Each' है।

questionText: Neither of the two boys / were willing to accept / the responsibility of the mistake. / No error
explanation:
'Neither of' takes a singular verb. Replace 'were' with 'was' in part (B).
उदा. 'Neither of', 'Either of' और 'Each of' के बाद plural noun/pronoun आता है लेकिन verb हमेशा singular होती है। इसलिए 'were' की जगह 'was' आएगा।

questionText: The teacher told the students / that honesty / was the best policy. / No error
explanation:
Universal truths and habitual facts always remain in the Simple Present tense, even if the reporting verb is in the past tense. Wait, exceptions exist for universal truths, but here 'Honesty is the best policy' is a universal truth, so 'was' should ideally be 'is'. Let's check typical SSC options: the correct part is (C) 'is the best policy'.

💡 **हिन्दी व्याख्या**: सही विकल्प '(D)' है। वाक्य के व्याकरणिक नियमों के अनुसार इसे शुद्ध किया गया है।

questionText: She is reading / the book / since two hours. / No error
explanation:
For a point of time, we use 'since' and for a period of time, we use 'for'. 'Two hours' is a period of time, so use 'for' instead of 'since'. Also, the tense should be present perfect continuous ('has been reading'). Therefore, part (A) contains the error.
उदा. निश्चित समय के लिए 'since' और अनिश्चित समय (अवधि) के लिए 'for' का प्रयोग होता है। 'Two hours' अवधि है, अतः 'Since' की जगह 'for' और Tense 'has been reading' होगा।

questionText: No sooner did the train arrive / at the station / than the passengers rushed into it. / No error
explanation:
The sentence is grammatically correct. 'No sooner' is correctly paired with 'did + V1' and 'than'.
उदा. वाक्य पूरी तरह से सही है। 'No sooner' के साथ 'did' (V1) और आगे 'than' का सही प्रयोग हुआ है।

questionText: One of my friends / are going to London / next week for higher studies. / No error
explanation:
'One of' is followed by a plural noun and a singular verb. Replace 'are' with 'is' in part (B).
उदा. 'One of' के बाद Plural Noun आता है लेकिन Verb हमेशा Singular होती है। अतः 'are' के स्थान पर 'is' का प्रयोग होगा।

questionText: Despite of his hard work, / he failed to secure / the first rank in the examination. / No error
explanation:
'Despite' does not take 'of' after it, whereas 'In spite' takes 'of'. Remove 'of' from part (A).
उदा. 'Despite' के साथ कभी भी 'of' का प्रयोग नहीं किया जाता है (जबकि 'In spite' के साथ 'of' आता है)। अतः (A) में 'of' का प्रयोग गलत है।

questionText: The committee / were divided / in their opinion regarding the issue. / No error
explanation:
When a collective noun like 'committee' shows division among its members, it takes a plural verb and plural pronoun ('their'). The sentence is correct.
उदा. जब सामूहिक संज्ञा (Collective Noun) में मतभेद दिखाया जाए, तो वह plural verb और plural pronoun लेती है। यहाँ 'were' और 'their' बिल्कुल सही हैं।

questionText: He asked me / that why I was / looking so sad. / No error
explanation:
In indirect speech for WH-questions, conjunctions like 'that' are not used before the question word. Remove 'that' from part (B).
उदा. Indirect Speech में Wh-word (why, what, etc.) से पहले 'that' का प्रयोग नहीं किया जाता है। अतः (B) में 'that' अतिरिक्त है।

questionText: Scarcely had he stepped / out of the house / than a heavy shower started. / No error
explanation:
'Scarcely' is followed by 'when' or 'before', not 'than'. Replace 'than' with 'when' in part (C).
उदा. 'Scarcely' के साथ जोड़ी 'when' की होती है न कि 'than' की। इसलिए (C) भाग में 'than' को 'when' से बदलें।

questionText: BRAVE
explanation:
'Brave' means ready to face and endure danger or pain; showing courage. Its antonym is 'Timid', which means showing a lack of courage or confidence.
उदा. 'Brave' का अर्थ साहसी होता है, इसका विलोम 'Timid' (डरपोक या संकोची) है।

questionText: TRANSITORY
explanation:
'Transitory' means lasting for a short time; 'Permanent' means lasting or remaining unchanged indefinitely. 
उदा. 'Transitory' का अर्थ क्षणिक या अल्पकालिक होता है, और 'Permanent' इसका विपरीत (स्थायी) है।

questionText: OSTENTATIOUS
explanation:
'Ostentatious' means designed to impress or attract notice (showy); 'Modest' means unassuming or moderate. 
उदा. 'Ostentatious' दिखावटी या आडंबरपूर्ण होता है, जबकि 'Modest' सादा और शालीन स्वभाव का होता है।

questionText: AMBIGUOUS
explanation:
'Ambiguous' means open to more than one interpretation (unclear); 'Clear' means easy to perceive, understand, or interpret. 
उदा. 'Ambiguous' अस्पष्ट या संदेहास्पद होता है, जबकि 'Clear' बिल्कुल स्पष्ट और पारदर्शी होता है।

questionText: scarce
explanation:
Rule in English: The antonym of an adjective is a word that has the opposite meaning. 
उदाहरण: "scarce" का विपरीत "abundant" होता है।

questionText: The politician's speech was ________.
explanation:
Rule in English: Find the word that means the opposite of the given adjective. 
उदाहरण: "candid" का विपरीत "evasive" है।

questionText: generous
explanation:
Rule in English: The antonym is a word that carries the opposite sense. 
उदाहरण: "generous" का विपरीत "selfish" है।

questionText: mature
explanation:
Rule in English: Find a word that means the opposite of the given adjective. 
उदाहरण: "mature" का विपरीत "immature" है।

questionText: fraudulent
explanation:
Rule in English: The opposite of a negative adjective is usually a positive one. 
उदाहरण: "fraudulent" का विपरीत "genuine" है।

questionText: scarcity
explanation:
Rule in English: The antonym of a noun indicating deficiency is a noun indicating plenty. 
उदाहरण: "scarcity" का विपरीत "abundance" है।

questionText: sincere
explanation:
Rule in English: Select the word that conveys the negative of the given adjective. 
उदाहरण: "sincere" का विपरीत "insincere" है।

questionText: tangible
explanation:
Rule in English: The opposite of a word denoting something that can be touched is one that cannot be touched. 
उदाहरण: "tangible" का विपरीत "intangible" है।

questionText: ancient
explanation:
Rule: An antonym is a word that has the opposite meaning of another word. For 'ancient', the opposite is 'modern'.
उदा. प्राचीन (ancient) का विपरीत शब्द 'modern' (आधुनिक) है।

questionText: benevolent
explanation:
Rule: The antonym of a word expresses the opposite quality. 'Benevolent' means well‑wishing; its antonym is 'malevolent', meaning ill‑wishing.
उदा. दयालु (benevolent) का विरोधी शब्द 'malevolent' (दुष्ट) है।

questionText: candid
explanation:
Rule: An antonym of an adjective signifies the opposite characteristic. 'Candid' means frank or open; its opposite is 'reserved', meaning not open.
उदा. ईमानदार (candid) का विपरीत शब्द 'reserved' (रुढ़िवादी) है।

questionText: diligent
explanation:
Rule: The opposite of a diligent person is one who is lazy. Hence, 'indolent' is the antonym of 'diligent'.
उदा. परिश्रमी (diligent) का विपरीत शब्द 'indolent' (आलसी) है।

questionText: elaborate
explanation:
Rule: To elaborate is to add details; to do the opposite is to simplify by removing details. Thus 'simplify' is the antonym.
उदा. विस्तार से बताना (elaborate) का विपरीत 'simplify' (सरल बनाना) है।

questionText: frugal
explanation:
Rule: 'Frugal' means economical and careful with money; its opposite is 'extravagant', meaning wasteful.
उदा. संयमी (frugal) का विपरीत शब्द 'extravagant' (भड़कीला) है।

questionText: genuine
explanation:
Rule: 'Genuine' means real or authentic; its opposite is 'counterfeit', meaning fake.
उदा. वास्तविक (genuine) का विपरीत शब्द 'counterfeit' (नकली) है।

questionText: humble
explanation:
Rule: 'Humble' means modest; the opposite is 'arrogant', meaning overly proud.
उदा. विनम्र (humble) का विपरीत शब्द 'arrogant' (अहंकारी) है।

questionText: incessant
explanation:
Rule: 'Incessant' means continuous or never ending; its opposite is 'intermittent', meaning occurring at intervals.
उदा. लगातार (incessant) का विपरीत शब्द 'intermittent' (विरामित) है।

questionText: juxtapose
explanation:
Rule: To juxtapose is to place together; the opposite action is to 'separate', meaning to keep apart.
उदा. तुलना के लिए बगल में रखना (juxtapose) का विपरीत 'separate' (अलग करना) है।

questionText: The ball is in your court
options: It is your turn to play in the match
You are responsible for taking the next step or decision
You have lost the game completely
The decision has been made by someone else
explanation:
The ball is in your court means it is up to you to make the next move or decision in a situation.
उदा. 'The ball is in your court' का अर्थ है - अब अगला कदम उठाने या निर्णय लेने की जिम्मेदारी आपकी है।

questionText: break the ice
options: To start a conversation in a new situation
To literally break ice for a ship
explanation:
Idioms are fixed expressions that convey a figurative meaning.
उदा. "We need to break the ice at the meeting so everyone feels comfortable." (हमें बैठक में सभी को सहज महसूस कराने के लिए 'आइस ब्रेक' करना है।)
grammarRule: Idioms are non‑literal phrases used to express a particular concept.

questionText: spill the beans
explanation:
The idiom means to disclose a secret or confidential information.
उदा. "He spilled the beans about the surprise party before the invitation went out." (उसने आश्चर्यजनक पार्टी के बारे में रहस्य फुसफुसा दिया।)
grammarRule: Idioms often use metaphorical language to convey hidden meanings.

questionText: A blessing in disguise
options: A situation that seems bad but turns out good
explanation:
It describes something that appears negative initially but ultimately turns beneficial.
उदा. "Losing his job was a blessing in disguise, leading him to pursue his passion." (उसका नौकरी खोना एक मोड़ था, जिससे उसने अपनी रुचि को आगे बढ़ाया।)
grammarRule: Idioms express contrast between appearance and reality.

questionText: under the weather
explanation:
It indicates a person is not feeling well.
उदा. "She stayed home because she was under the weather." (वह बीमार होने के कारण घर पर रही।)
grammarRule: Idioms often use natural elements to describe health or mood.

questionText: Cost an arm and a leg
explanation:
The idiom indicates a very high cost.
उदा. "The new smartphone cost an arm and a leg, so I bought the older model." (नया स्मार्टफोन बहुत महँगा था, इसलिए मैंने पुराना मॉडल खरीदा।)
grammarRule: Idioms use exaggerated comparison to emphasize cost or effort.

questionText: kick the bucket
explanation:
It is a euphemistic way of saying someone has died.
उदा. "He passed away last night, it was a quiet kick the bucket." (वह कल रात गुजर गया, यह एक शांत मृत्यु थी।)
grammarRule: Idioms can serve as euphemisms for sensitive topics.

questionText: bite the bullet
explanation:
It means to accept a difficult or unpleasant situation with courage.
उदा. "He decided to bite the bullet and apologize to his friend." (उसने साहस से अपने दोस्त से माफी माँगने का फैसला किया।)
grammarRule: Idioms can imply stoic acceptance of adversity.

questionText: Throw in the towel
explanation:
It means to give up or admit defeat.
उदा. "After six attempts, she threw in the towel and sought help." (छः प्रयासों के बाद, उसने हार मान ली और मदद मांगी।)
grammarRule: Idioms use sports terminology to express resignation.

questionText: to beat around the bush
options: Talk about a bush in a garden
Physically beat a bush with a stick
Speak loudly in a quiet place
explanation:
The idiom "to beat around the bush" means to avoid addressing the main topic directly.
इस मुहावरे का मतलब मुख्य विषय को सीधे संबोधित करने से बचना है।

questionText: let the cat out of the bag
options: Physically releasing a cat from a bag
Selling a bag of cat food
Hiding a cat in a bag
explanation:
The idiom "let the cat out of the bag" means to reveal a secret or surprise.
इस मुहावरे का मतलब एक रहस्य या आश्चर्य को उजागर करने से है।

questionText: once in a blue moon
options: A blue moon that occurs every year
Every time there is a blue moon
A moon that is always blue
explanation:
"Once in a blue moon" refers to something that happens very rarely.
यह मुहावरा ऐसे किसी घटना को दर्शाता है जो बहुत कम ही होती है।

questionText: the ball is in your court
options: You have a physical ball to play with
Responsibility lies with you to act
You need to keep the ball in your possession
You must play a sport with a ball
explanation:
"The ball is in your court" means that the responsibility to act or decide lies with you.
इस मुहावरे का मतलब है कि निर्णय लेने या कार्रवाई करने की जिम्मेदारी आपके हाथ में है।

questionText: to burn the midnight oil
options: To physically burn oil at midnight
To work late into the night
To light oil lamps after midnight
explanation:
"To burn the midnight oil" means to work late into the night, often studying or working on a task.
इस मुहावरे का अर्थ है रात देर तक काम करना या पढ़ाई करना।

questionText: a piece of cake
options: A cake that is broken into pieces
explanation:
"A piece of cake" indicates that something is easy to do or accomplish.
इस मुहावरे का मतलब है कि कोई कार्य या गतिविधि बहुत आसान है।

questionText: under the weather
explanation:
"Under the weather" figuratively means feeling ill or unwell.
इस मुहावरे का मतलब है कि व्यक्ति अस्वस्थ या बीमार महसूस कर रहा है।

questionText: hit the nail on the head
options: To physically hit a nail on its head
To give a correct or accurate answer
To hit a nail but not on the head
explanation:
"Hit the nail on the head" means to give a correct or accurate answer or to identify the exact issue.
इस मुहावरे का अर्थ है सही या सटीक उत्तर देना या समस्या को ठीक से पहचानना।

questionText: let sleeping dogs lie
options: Keeping dogs asleep during the day
Avoiding stirring up old or unresolved issues
Letting dogs sleep in a cage
Sleeping dogs that are physically lying down
explanation:
"Let sleeping dogs lie" means to avoid bringing up old or unresolved issues that could cause trouble.
इस मुहावरे का मतलब है पुराने या अनसुलझे मुद्दों को और न बढ़ाना।

questionText: add fuel to the fire
options: Adding actual fuel to a fire
Worsening an already tense or volatile situation
explanation:
"Add fuel to the fire" means to worsen an already tense or volatile situation by making it more intense.
इस मुहावरे का अर्थ है किसी तंग या गर्म स्थिति को और भी खराब करना।

questionText: After months of negotiations, the parties finally decided to ___ and move forward with the merger.
explanation:
The idiom means to reach a mutual agreement and move forward. It is used when parties resolve differences and settle on a solution.
